reason: Inflorescences 3-20(-30)-flowered: number of flowers per inflorescence is 3-20, sometimes up to 30. The container and the extreme value are both right.
Stem colour given as alternatives: purplish brown, blackish or yellow-brown. 'Brown' is a broader but true reading of 'purplish brown', and 'black' is fine for 'blackish'.
'Rameaux assez divergents' means rather spreading branches, so spreading (PATO_0104356) on branch is right.

'Inflorescences subombellées' means nearly umbel-like inflorescences, so umbelliform (FLOPO_0991031) is right. An 'approximately' qualifier for 'sub-' would be better but is not needed for the statement to be true.

fix: 'Subglabrous' was reduced to 'glabrous'. The FLOPO class subglabrous already exists, so map the word 'subglabrous' to it rather than dropping the 'sub-' prefix.
reason: The stem base is nearly hairless, not hairless. The bearer, stem base, is right.

fix: Two causes. (1) 'Villous' was mapped to the generic 'pubescent hair' although FLOPO_0991051 villous exists. (2) The frequency word in 'but occasionally glabrous except on veins' belongs to the other alternative (glabrous), not to 'villous'. Do not copy a frequency word across 'but' to the earlier value.
reason: The abaxial side of the leaf blade is densely villous as a rule. The annotation calls it 'occasionally' pubescent, which turns the usual state into the rare one.

fix: In conifers, 'seed cone' must map to megasporangiate strobilus, as the previous review decided for 'seed cone' (C378), and never to fruit.
reason: Cupressus has seed cones, not fruits. The shape 'oblong-globose' as a continuum is otherwise right.
Stipules 0.3-1.2 cm long.
Bracts glabrous or loosely hairy: taxon-level alternatives, with 'loosely' read as 'sparsely'.
Branches more or less glandular-tubercled: tuberculate with 'approximately' is right. 'Glandular' is left out, but the annotation is still true.
3-5 spikes at each node of the inflorescence. The per-node position with stem node as landmark is acceptable.
Stamens shorter than the corolla.

fix: 'Fragrant' is a synonym of sweet-scented (FLOPO_0991016), so 'not fragrant' should negate sweet-scented. Negating the generic 'odorous' says the flower has no smell at all, which is more than 'not fragrant' says.
reason: 'Not fragrant' denies a pleasant scent. It does not deny every odour.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on inflorescence axis (PO_0020122), colour reddish brown
fix: In 'ferruginous-tomentulose', 'ferruginous' gives the colour of the hairs, not of the axis. A colour joined by a hyphen to a hair word should go to the hairs (trichome), with the part (here the inflorescence axis) as the whole. 'Ferruginous' (rust-coloured) is also better read as reddish brown than orange.
reason: The thyrse axes are covered with short rust-coloured hairs. The axes themselves are not orange.
Flowers white.
Bracts with a cuspidate apex.
Racemes in pairs: 2 racemes.
Blade usually unlobed: lobed, negated, with 'usually'.

fix: 'Glandular hairy' could map to the more specific glandular-pubescent (FLOPO_0991173).
reason: These are the calyx lobes (the text before them, 'unequally 5-lobed to the base', describes the calyx), and they are hairy. 'Hairy' is broader than 'glandular hairy' but still true.
Inner sepals 3-veined: 3 veins in the sepal. Vascular bundle has 'vein' as a synonym.
Seeds numerous: present, with the count word 'many'.

The statement in the middle of the context, 'Leaf sheaths glabrous; auricles absent', gives leaf sheath auricles absent. The earlier 'auricles absent' is about the culm sheath and should get a culm-sheath bearer if it is annotated separately.
Leaf apex obtuse-rounded: obtuse is a true reading of the joined term.

target: lobe of the keel crest; whole: keel petal (PO_0025326)
fix: In 'keel ..., crest 2-parted, with 2–3 lobes on each side', the lobes belong to the crest of the keel petal. 'Lobes' after a flower part must not default to leaf lamina lobe. Take the nearest part named before 'lobes' as the whole.
reason: These are 2-3 lobes on each side of the keel crest of a Polygala flower, not leaf lamina lobes.
Lamina triangular-pentagonal, read as a continuum of 2-D shapes.
Pedicel of the female flowers ± pubescent: pubescent with 'approximately'.
Perennial herb or subshrub: habit alternatives, herbaceous or suffrutescent.
Sepals elliptic or ovate.
6-9 secondary veins on each side of the midvein.
Filaments about as long as the anthers: length ratio 1, with 'approximately'.
